title: English Grammar & Vocabulary Practice Task
description: Comprehensive practice task covering all 8 supported question types including multiple choice, true/false, fill in the blanks, matching, ordering, short answer, and essay writing.
instructions: Answer all questions carefully. Objective questions are graded automatically upon submission, while essay responses are reviewed by your instructor.

questions.text: Which of the following sentences uses the Present Perfect tense correctly?

options.text: She has visited London three times this year.
She is visit London every summer.

questions.explanation: The Present Perfect tense is formed with has/have + past participle ('has visited') for actions in an unfinished time period ('this year').

questions.text: Select ALL words below that are synonyms of the adjective 'diligent':
questions.explanation: 'Hardworking', 'industrious', and 'conscientious' all describe careful, persistent effort, whereas 'negligent' is an antonym.

questions.text: In English grammar, an adverb can modify a verb, an adjective, or another adverb.
questions.explanation: Adverbs modify verbs ('runs quickly'), adjectives ('very tall'), or other adverbs ('quite easily').

questions.text: What is the irregular past participle form of the verb 'write'?
questions.explanation: The principal parts are write (base) -> wrote (past simple) -> written (past participle).

questions.text: Complete the conditional sentence: If I _____ known about the meeting earlier, I would _____ attended it.
questions.explanation: Third conditional structure: If + subject + had + past participle, subject + would + have + past participle.

questions.text: Match each linguistic term on the left with its correct definition on the right:

pairs.right: A word with the same or nearly the same meaning
A word opposite in meaning to another
A word pronounced the same as another but differing in meaning

correct_answer.P1: A word with the same or nearly the same meaning
correct_answer.P2: A word opposite in meaning to another
correct_answer.P3: A word pronounced the same as another but differing in meaning

questions.explanation: Synonyms share meaning, antonyms have opposite meanings, and homophones share pronunciation.
